description: One trained model Volume Vision produced, and the one fact Volume Vision has no reason to hold: whether it is the model an iOS app should be pulling right now for one company and one piecework activity. get_active_model is what a scanning app queries to find out; activate_model is what moves the flag, and it auto-deprecates whichever model held it before — only one model per (company, piecework_activity) is ever Active at a time. attach_model_file gives a record the binary itself, uploaded once from Volume Vision; get_model_file_chunk is how an iOS app then reads it back from ERPNext rather than from Volume Vision directly.

fields.description: The series an ML Model is named from, expanded by the controller rather than by Frappe's naming_series hook so a docname is the same shape on a bench and in the standalone suite — MLM-2026-0001. The year is the year the model was registered.
fields.label: Series

fields.description: The human name for this model — 'Cherry Fill Detection'. Several versions of the same model share this name; version is what tells them apart.
fields.label: Model Name

fields.description: Digits and dots — '3.2', '1' — matching Volume Vision's own TrainedModel.version, which is a training counter rather than a package version.
fields.label: Version

fields.description: Draft is registered but not deployed. Active is the one model of its (company, piecework_activity) pair that get_active_model returns — activate_model is the only way in, and it auto-deprecates whatever was Active before. Deprecated is a superseded model, kept for the record. Archived is retired by hand and excluded from get_active_model even if nothing ever replaced it.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The company this deployment decision belongs to. The same trained model can be registered once per company that runs it, each activated independently.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: What this model is used for — 'bucket_fill_detection', 'harvest_quality', 'inspection_aid'. Together with company this is the pair get_active_model is queried by, and the pair activate_model enforces one Active model against.
fields.label: Piecework Activity

fields.description: Which apps pull this model — comma-separated: 'BucketLog', 'FarmOps', or 'Both'.
fields.label: Deployment Targets

fields.description: The Volume Vision TrainedModel.uuid this record tracks — the key iOS apps use to identify a locally cached model. Empty for a model registered without a Volume Vision source.
fields.label: Source UUID

fields.description: The Volume Vision instance this model was trained on, e.g. 'http://umbrel.local:8095'. Not where an iOS app downloads it from — that is GET /api/sync/models/<uuid>/download against whichever server the app already syncs with.
fields.label: Source Server

fields.description: What kind of model this is.
fields.label: Model Kind

fields.description: The file format an iOS app expects to load. CoreML is what BucketLog and Farm Ops run on-device.
fields.label: Model Format

fields.description: The compiled model binary this record owns, uploaded once via attach_model_file (from Volume Vision or elsewhere) and served from ERPNext after — get_model_file_chunk is what an iOS app reads it back through. Empty until attach_model_file has run. Set programmatically; there is nothing to type here.
fields.label: Model File

fields.description: Where this record's class_names came from. A model attached as a bundle (a zip carrying model.mlmodel beside a manifest.json written by Volume Vision at export time) says 'class_names source: bundle manifest from VV training' and names the uuid it came from; anything else says the labels were entered on this site. Set by attach_model_file and pull_model_from_vv; there is nothing to type here.
fields.label: Manifest Source

fields.description: The bundle's manifest.json, verbatim, when the attached file is a bundle — empty when it is a raw model. It is stored whole because it carries two things this doctype has no column for and an iOS app needs at inference time: preprocessing (input_size, normalization, color space) and class_roles. get_active_model hands both back under manifest.metadata.bundle so a phone reads them without unpacking the zip. Set programmatically; there is nothing to type here.
fields.label: Bundle Manifest

fields.description: The taxonomy schema_name class_names belongs to — which controlled vocabulary of labels this model's outputs are drawn from.
fields.label: Taxonomy Schema

fields.description: The taxonomy schema's version, so a caller can tell whether this model's labels match the taxonomy a client currently has cached.
fields.label: Taxonomy Version

fields.description: The ordered label array this model was trained to predict, as a JSON array — matches Volume Vision's class_names_json and is what an iOS client's manifest parser reads to map an output index back to a label.
fields.label: Class Names

fields.description: Training metrics as a JSON object — accuracy, mAP, loss, whatever Volume Vision recorded for this training run.
fields.label: Metrics

fields.description: The model file's size in bytes, as reported by Volume Vision.
fields.label: File Size (Bytes)

fields.description: When training finished in Volume Vision.
fields.label: Training Completed At

fields.description: When activate_model last set this record's status to Active. Empty for a model that has never been activated.
fields.label: Deployed At

fields.description: Anything about this model's rollout worth reading later — why it was activated, what regressed in the version before it, what to watch for in the field.
fields.label: Notes

name: ML Model
